claims.text: Order.Ship() refuses any order that is not paid by throwing OrderStatusException; the public constructor, called by PlaceOrderAsync, refuses an empty item list. Both decide from the order's own fields only.
ShipOrderAsync finds the order, calls order.Ship(), then notifier.Send, then SaveChangesAsync; it contains no status check of its own.

StaffOnly is a policy registered in Program.cs (RequireRole("staff")); [Authorize(Policy = "StaffOnly")] makes ASP.NET Core evaluate it before the action runs; a failing caller gets 403 (401 with no token) and the action is not called.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs: Policy-based authorization; Filters (authorization filters run first); OrdersController.cs:88-90 comment

claims.text: OrdersController.Cancel loads an untracked (read-only) copy with FindForReadingAsync only to run AuthorizeAsync(User, existing, "OrderOwner") (OrderOwnerHandler), returns Forbid() on failure, then calls CancelOrderAsync, where Order.Cancel() decides.
OrderOwnerHandler succeeds for a caller in role staff, or for a caller whose customer row (found via ICustomerRepository.FindByIdentitySubjectAsync with the token's sub) has Id == order.CustomerId.

OrdersController.Ship's body is one call to ShipOrderAsync and Ok(ToDto(order)); no line in OrdersController checks Status (ToDto and List only copy it into DTOs). OrderStatusException becomes 409 in ExceptionHandlingMiddleware.
ProductsController.List queries DonHangDbContext directly (no repository, no domain method), as its comment says: it has no rule to apply.
Order.Ship() takes no parameters; Order has no access to the request or the caller's token; roles are read in DonHang.Api (StaffOnly policy, OrderOwnerHandler).

claims.text: Placement rule: a rule decided from one order's own fields belongs in Order; steps reaching outside the order stay in OrderService; who may act is decided in DonHang.Api; the controller only translates HTTP. A status check in a controller takes a rule out of Order.
A domain model is worth its extra methods when a class has rules that several use cases must respect; an operation with no rule, such as listing products, stays simpler as a direct query.
